evals.prompt: I spent last weekend debugging a Cilium network policy that silently ate my database operator's API-server traffic. I have my notes and the fix. Help me turn this into a blog post.
assertions: Asks framing questions before drafting: post type, target reader, and the one concrete lesson
Gathers or requests first-hand evidence (log lines, timestamps, the actual fix diff) into a research file before outlining
Proposes 2-3 opening hook alternatives rather than a single opener
Draft leads with the payoff in the first three sentences instead of chronological backstory

evals.prompt: My post about self-hosting a CI runner fleet is finished and published on my Substack. Now I want to get it onto Hacker News, LinkedIn, and dev.to.
assertions: HN guidance: submit the canonical URL with the original de-hyped title, never solicit votes, be present in comments
LinkedIn variant is a native standalone-value post with the hook in the first ~2 lines and the external link kept out of the body
dev.to variant sets canonical_url frontmatter pointing at the Substack original and uses at most 4 tags
Advises adapting each variant rather than pasting the same text to all three platforms

evals.prompt: Here's my blog post draft. Before I publish, can you edit it? It needs to not sound like it was written by an AI.
assertions: Runs distinct single-dimension edit passes rather than one combined rewrite
Identifies AI-tell clusters (generic openings, buzz-verbs, symmetric structure, em-dash density) with specific instances from the draft
Preserves the author's voice and colorful lines; does not flag isolated tells or rewrite quoted text
Adds or requests first-hand specifics (numbers, anecdotes, opinions) rather than only deleting flagged phrases

evals.prompt: Write an ADR documenting our decision to switch from Loki to VictoriaLogs.
assertions: The blog-writer skill does not trigger; ADR authoring is not blog writing
